content: Cefuroxime is a cephalosporin antibiotic used to treat a variety of bacterial infections. It is not effective against viral infections such as the common cold or flu. This medication should be taken orally as directed by your doctor, typically twice daily (every 12 hours). To enhance absorption and minimize stomach upset, take cefuroxime with food. Swallow the tablets whole; do not crush or chew them, as they have a strong bitter taste. For optimal effectiveness, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue taking the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or stomach pain. Dizziness and drowsiness may also occur, particularly at higher doses. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, cefuroxime may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Before taking cefuroxime, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to penicillins, or to other cephalosporin antibiotics (e.g., cephalexin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. This drug may cause dizziness or drowsiness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. Cefuroxime may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine). During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Cefuroxime may interfere with certain lab tests (e.g., diabetic urine tests, blood glucose tests), potentially causing false results. If someone overdoses and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
